tools.name: peers
tools.title: List Peers
tools.description: List the AI sessions (Claude Code / Codex conversations) of your own user that you can message with send, and your own profile; your client's own agent list (such as ListAgents) does not show them. Each profile says which machine the conversation runs on: hostname, platform (darwin, linux, wsl or win32), environment (the WSL distribution, else "") and utcOffset (local time minus UTC, in minutes), as its hooks report them with every event, and the label it set with set_profile. Offline ones only with includeOffline. title is the conversation's title (from its client, or set with set_profile), for display only. status: listening (waiting for messages, answers right away), working or idle (sees a message when its user next sends a prompt or it next calls a tool), or offline (ended, or no activity for 30 minutes).

includeOffline.description: Also list offline sessions active in the last 24 hours

title.description: The conversation's title as its client shows it, or as set with set_profile; for display only (send takes the name or id)

hostname.description: The machine the conversation runs on, as its hooks report it (without a .local suffix)

platform.description: The operating system of that machine; wsl is a Linux distribution under Windows

environment.description: Tells environments that share the host name apart: the WSL distribution; "" otherwise

utcOffset.description: The machine's local time minus UTC, in minutes

label.description: A short machine label the session set with set_profile, shown in place of the hostname; "" when none

tools.name: send
tools.title: Send Direct Message
tools.description: Send a direct message to one AI session of your own user (an id or name listed by peers); for a meeting or the global chat use send_message instead. The recipient gets the whole message in its notification; to answer a message you received, use reply. Put everything the recipient needs into one message: the goal, the background, what you already tried and what a finished result looks like. Then end your turn rather than polling with read: the answer reaches you through the hooks after your next tool call or at the end of a turn (at your user's next prompt once the automatic-turn limit is reached); notifyWhenIdle tells you when the recipient finishes its turn. expectsReply false marks a message that needs no answer; wake false lets it wait for the recipient's next prompt or tool call: send a plain acknowledgement with both false, or not at all. Needs the n2n-nexus hooks.

to.description: Session id, or the name of a session that is not offline, from peers

text.description: Plain text, shown whole in the recipient's notification (a long message is cut there, and read returns it).

notifyWhenIdle.description: Get one notice when the recipient next finishes its turn or goes offline

expectsReply.description: false: tell the recipient no reply is needed (for results, notices, acknowledgements).

wake.description: false: do not wake the recipient or hold its turn; it sees the message at its next prompt or tool call (for acknowledgements and other messages that can wait).

tools.name: read
tools.title: Read Direct Messages
tools.description: Read your unread direct messages from other AI sessions of your own user, oldest first, and mark them read; meetings and the global chat are read with read_messages instead. A notification shows each message whole; one that needs no reply is marked read there when the notification comes with a prompt, and every message shown whole is when it wakes you or holds your Stop. read returns the ones cut or not shown, those shown after a tool call, and those shown with a prompt that you have not answered yet. When a message asks for an answer (expectsReply true), answer once with reply.

remaining.description: Unread messages left after this batch

tools.name: reply
tools.title: Reply to Message
tools.description: Reply to a direct message you received (for a meeting or the global chat use send_message instead); it goes to the original sender, and the message you answer counts as read. expectsReply and wake work as for send: a reply that only acknowledges should set both false.

messageId.description: A message you received, from a notification or read

text.description: Plain text, shown whole in the recipient's notification (a long message is cut there, and read returns it).

expectsReply.description: false: tell the recipient no reply is needed (for results, notices, acknowledgements).

wake.description: false: do not wake the recipient or hold its turn; it sees the message at its next prompt or tool call (for acknowledgements and other messages that can wait).

tools.name: listen

tools.description: on: after each turn, wait up to about 10 minutes for new direct messages and continue when one arrives (in Claude Code your user can press Esc to stop one wait). off: stop.

tools.name: send_message
tools.title: Post Message
tools.description: Post to a meeting or to the global chat; a direct message to one session is send (or reply). Post to a meeting (meetingId, else the active meeting) or, when no meeting is active, to the shared global chat that every session can read with read_messages. The sender is this conversation's session id (claude:<id> / codex:<id>) when the n2n-nexus hooks are installed, else the MCP adapter instance; identity says which. messageId is the message's number in its meeting (from 1), or its global chat id. draft: true publishes the message as the meeting's current draft (a PROPOSAL; currentProposalId is its number): its required approvers are the members that are required approvers and conversation sessions at that moment, and the members take a stance on it with stance. Only a draft replaces the current draft and starts its stances afresh; a PROPOSAL sent without draft changes neither. Before posting to a meeting, read what others said: when messages of others came after you last read the meeting (read_messages in unread mode, a notification that showed them whole, or an earlier refusal; history reads do not count), the message is not sent: ok is false, refused true and unread has those messages, which now count as read. Take them into account rather than resending the same text. The next send_message to that meeting goes through even if more messages arrived, with a note of the unread numbers appended to its text; a draft or a DECISION never does: it is posted only once everything is read. Global chat has no such check.

category.description: Optional label. DECISION is also added to the meeting's decisions list. Omitted = no category.

meetingId.description: Target meeting. Defaults to the active meeting, or global chat when none is active.

draft.description: Publish as the meeting's current draft for the members to endorse or object to (meetings only; category is PROPOSAL, any other category fails).

unread.description: The messages of others you had not read, oldest first, texts together cut to the notification limit; those attached whole now count as read.

cut.description: The text was cut to fit; read_messages returns it whole.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.title: Read Chat / Meeting Messages
tools.description: Read a meeting or the global chat; your direct messages are read with read. Read global chat (default) or one meeting's messages (meetingId). Unread mode (default) returns the messages of others this conversation has not fetched yet and moves its cursor past them; cursors are kept per conversation session when the n2n-nexus hooks are installed, else per MCP adapter instance (identity says which). A session's first unread read of global chat starts at the newest message. Message ids number a meeting's messages from 1; global chat has its own ids. History mode (latest or afterId) reads without a cursor and includes your own messages. Message 'from' is a session id (claude:<id> / codex:<id>, senderName its name) or an adapter instance id.

count.description: Most messages to return (oldest first; with latest, the newest).

meetingId.description: Meeting to read; omit for global chat.

latest.description: History mode: the newest count messages, oldest first. Moves no cursor. Not with afterId.

afterId.description: History mode: the first count messages with an id above afterId (in a meeting, its message number). Moves no cursor. Not with latest.

senderName.description: The sending session's name when it posted; null for an adapter instance

senderMachine.description: The sending session's machine when it posted, "<label or hostname> · <platform>[ <environment>]"; null for an adapter instance

senderBackfilled.description: senderName and senderMachine were filled in when the database was upgraded, from the session as it was then, not when the message was posted

tools.description: List meetings, newest first: id, topic, status, initiator, participants (everyone who has posted), members (who has joined and not left: name, conversation title and machine as they were when it joined, mode, approver, session status, wakes the meeting caused), message/decision counts, summary, endReason (manual: end_meeting; consensus: every required approver endorsed the current draft; expired: the host closed it after meetingRetentionDays without a message) and proposal: the current draft (messageId, author), the version of its required approver list and its approvals (required, endorsed, waiting: required approvers without a stance, objections), null when no draft was published. Initiator, participants and members are conversation session ids (claude:<id> / codex:<id>) when the n2n-nexus hooks are installed, else MCP adapter instance ids. Read messages with read_messages(meetingId).

tools.name: start_meeting
tools.title: Start Meeting
tools.description: Start a meeting and return its id. It becomes the active meeting that send_message and end_meeting use when no meetingId is given. The initiator (this conversation's session id when the n2n-nexus hooks are installed, else the MCP adapter instance) joins it as an active, required member. seat "user": you take the user's seat (see stance).

seat.description: Take the user's seat: this conversation acts for the user (one seat per meeting; taking it moves it from whoever held it). Needs the n2n-nexus hooks.

tools.name: end_meeting
tools.title: End Meeting
tools.description: End a meeting (default: the active one) with an optional summary; its history is then read-only. In a meeting with the user's seat only the seat ends it, with a summary (required: what was decided, what was not, who does what next); an end_meeting by anyone else is posted to the meeting as a proposal to end it, ok false, refused true, messageId its number.

summary.description: Outcome of the meeting, kept with it.

tools.name: join_meeting
tools.title: Join Meeting
tools.description: Join an active meeting, or change how you take part in it. mode active (default): new messages of others wake this conversation; async: you see them at your next prompt or tool call. approver: whether your approval is required for a decision (default: required when active, optional when async). since sets where read_messages starts for this meeting: beginning, latest (default on the first join) or after a message number. delivery says how you will be told about new messages: wake, next-hook, or unavailable (no n2n-nexus hooks, so nothing can notify you). Switch to async to pause; leave_meeting to stop. seat "user": you take the user's seat (see stance); the session that held it stays a member.

mode.description: active: woken by new messages of others; async: see them at your next hook.

approver.description: Whether your approval is required for a decision. Default: required when active, optional when async.

since.description: Where read_messages starts for this meeting: beginning, latest, or after this message number (0: the beginning). Default on the first join: latest; on a later join the cursor stays.

seat.description: Take the user's seat: this conversation acts for the user (one seat per meeting; taking it moves it from whoever held it). Needs the n2n-nexus hooks.

tools.name: leave_meeting
tools.title: Leave Meeting
tools.description: Leave a meeting: its new messages no longer notify or wake you and your approval is no longer counted. Notices about stances on your proposals remain available at your next normal hook, but do not wake you after leaving. join_meeting joins again; reopen_meeting does not.

tools.name: stance
tools.title: Take Stance
tools.description: Endorse or object to a PROPOSAL of an active meeting (messageId: its number in the meeting), or withdraw your stance on it. You have one stance per proposal; a new one replaces it. object needs a note with the reason and also posts it to the meeting; the proposal's author is told of every stance. When the proposal is the meeting's current draft (published with send_message draft) and it has at least 2 required approvers, every one of them endorsed it and nobody objects to it, the meeting closes by consensus: a DECISION with the draft is posted and decided is true. An MCP adapter instance (no n2n-nexus hooks) cannot approve (counted: false), but its objection blocks like any other. approvals are the proposal's: required (its required approvers, empty unless it is the current draft), endorsed, waiting (required approvers without a stance) and objections. Read first: when messages of others came after you last read the meeting, an endorse or object is refused (ok false, refused true, unread has those messages, which now count as read); take the stance again once you have weighed them. A withdraw goes through and carries them in unread. With the user's seat (start_meeting or join_meeting with seat "user"), the seat decides: its endorse of the current draft makes the host post a DECISION with the draft (listing objections still open) and clears the draft; its object voids the draft; the meeting stays open for the next point. Consensus of the others then decides nothing; the host only posts when it is reached or lost. Only the seat ends such a meeting. An object, and a stance that changes your last one on the proposal, need grounds in the note: #n of a message of this meeting, a file path, a URL, or a sentence starting with 实测：/文档：/数据： (Measured:/Docs:/Data:); only the form is checked. You may change your stance on a proposal at most twice; withdraw always works. The seat is held to neither, and its object is not refused for unread messages. decisionId is the DECISION the seat's endorsement posted.

messageId.description: The proposal's number in the meeting.

seat.description: The user's seat and its stance on the proposal, null in a meeting without a seat. The seat is in none of the other lists.

unread.description: The messages of others you had not read, oldest first, texts together cut to the notification limit; those attached whole now count as read.

cut.description: The text was cut to fit; read_messages returns it whole.

tools.name: host_maintenance
tools.title: Clean Up the Host
tools.description: Host housekeeping. 'prune' removes the oldest count global chat messages (count ≥ 1 required), 'clear' removes all of them. 'cleanup' runs the hourly cleanup now: tasks past their TTL fail; finished tasks, events, read or expired direct messages, delivered notices, adapter instances not seen and sessions not active for retentionDays go (a session a direct message still references stays); an active meeting without a message for meetingRetentionDays since its last message, start or reopening closes with endReason expired; a meeting closed or archived meetingRetentionDays ago goes with its messages, decisions, stances and members. With dryRun true it changes nothing and reports what it would do. 'export' returns meeting meetingId as markdown: state, members, decisions and messages with who wrote them and on which machine.

count.description: prune: how many of the oldest global messages to remove (≥ 1). Ignored by clear.

dryRun.description: cleanup: report what would be removed or changed without changing anything. Ignored by the other actions.

meetingId.description: export: the meeting to export (required). Ignored by the other actions.

removed.description: prune and clear: global messages removed.

remaining.description: prune and clear: global messages left.

cleanup.description: cleanup: what was removed or changed, or with dryRun would be. counts: tasksExpired (failed for their TTL), tasks, events, meetingsExpired (closed), meetings (deleted), messagesExpired (unread direct messages marked expired), messages, notices, toolUseBindings, sessions, instances.
